outline: 172 Inequalities with Variables in the Denominator

examples.solution_text:
Absolute value is non-negative, so it can be at most zero only when its argument is zero.
$\begin{aligned}x-4&=0\\x&=4\end{aligned}$
The solution is $\{4\}$.

Absolute value is non-negative, so it cannot be less than $-3$.
There is no solution: $\varnothing$.

examples.derivation: |x-2|≤4 gives -4≤x-2≤4, hence -2≤x≤6 and [-2,6]. The graph y=|x-2| has vertex (2,0) and intersects y=4 at (-2,4) and (6,4), matching both projections and the included endpoints.
|x-2|>3 gives x-2<-3 or x-2>3, hence x<-1 or x>5. The solution is (-∞,-1)∪(5,∞). The number line correctly places open endpoints at -1 and 5 and arrows towards the outside regions.
Non-negativity forces |x-4|=0. Thus x-4=0, x=4, and the solution is {4}. No diagram is necessary.
|x+2|≥0 for every real x, so |x+2|<-3 is impossible. The solution is ∅. No diagram is necessary.

The domain requires x≠2. Reciprocating the positive quantities in 1/|x-2|≤1/4 gives |x-2|≥4. Thus x-2≤-4 or x-2≥4, giving x≤-2 or x≥6 and (-∞,-2]∪[6,∞). This excludes x=2. The number line correctly shows closed endpoints and outside directions.
